- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips sharply, delay or dampen forecast adjustment for 1–2 periods.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish” sentiment followed by price correction, model tends to miss the correction; add a 2–5% downward bias in forecast for 3–5 days post-sentiment peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), apply a “reversion bias” — forecast should be 1–3% below model for next 3–5 days unless sentiment shifts.
